hook.line: 'This is crazy. Yesterday was Adobe. Today, it's Microsoft.'
hook.visual: Selfie close-up in a car, red 'Goodbye Microsoft' label with emoji pinned above his head, small yellow-highlight captions, hand counting on fingers by 2.62 s.

beats.what: Car selfie, red title label 'Goodbye Microsoft' on top; first word at 0 s
Finger counting gesture on 'yesterday it was Adobe' links to the previous viral video
Promise: free open-source copies so you never pay another subscription
Cut to a screenshot of the repo notes listing WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft
Back to face for 'AI built the system, he wrote it in Rust, and it's free'
One raised finger on 'one developer' vs Microsoft's spend
Thesis: the future is custom software for niche markets, learn to vibe code
Pitch for his AI Builders community in his profile
Ends mid-energy on selling software to the masses

why_it_works: Series framing ('yesterday Adobe, today Microsoft') makes the video feel like the next episode of a story viewers already saw
Comment-keyword offer for the GitHub repo early in the video turns viewers into commenters (3,122 comments, the highest here)
A persistent red title label tells scrollers the topic even with sound off, for the whole 97 s
He takes a personal position (shorting software stocks), which invites agreement and argument in comments
weaknesses: Two cuts in 97 s (longest shot 67 s); nothing visual changes apart from his hands
The only proof, the repo screenshot, is on screen for about 5 s
Captions are small and low-contrast against the jumper
Three different CTAs (comment for repo, profile, community) compete with each other
for_robert: Copy the persistent topic label above the head and the comment-keyword offer, but avoid the 67 s unbroken shot: have Fred swim in with the proof screenshot instead of a hard cut.
